shipped_default_operating_point.name: balanced_top5
shipped_default_operating_point.selection_rule: Pre-hoc, named rule (fixed during port, applied without re-inspecting comparative holdout performance): first operating point, in the fixed candidate order active_top10 -> balanced_top5 -> selective_top2 -> sniper_top1, satisfying ALL of (a) n > 100, (b) positive avg net return/trade, (c) Wilson-95% lower bound within reach of 50%.
shipped_default_operating_point.why_balanced_top5: n=111 (>100); avg net return/trade +0.17% (positive); Wilson95=[45.7%, 63.9%] (lower bound close to 50%). First candidate to clear all three.
shipped_default_operating_point.why_not_active_top10: n=320 (>100, ok) but avg net return/trade is -0.05% -- fails the positive-expectancy condition.
shipped_default_operating_point.why_not_selective_top2_or_sniper_top1: n=34 and n=11 respectively -- both fail the n>100 condition regardless of their (higher, but noisier) win rates.
shipped_default_operating_point.fixes_prior_process: MODEL.md previously narrated 'balanced' as though chosen by eyeballing holdout profit factor across all four points -- a mild form of holdout-peeking on WHICH threshold to ship (the threshold VALUES themselves were and remain leak-free: quantile_source=train_oof_pooled, computed from train-only OOF quantiles). This field replaces that narrative with an explicit, falsifiable, pre-hoc rule that resolves to the same point.

note: Thresholds live in this file (derived from train OOF raw-score quantiles, quantile_source=train_oof_pooled -- leak-free). active_top10/selective_top2/sniper_top1 remain available below (operating_point_quantiles) for transparency only; they are not the shipped default. See MODEL.md for full detail and the runtime-gating caveat.
